text: Why does one tenth not terminate in binary?
choices: Its denominator has a prime factor of 5, and 5 does not divide 2
Because floating point has only 52 bits of fraction
Because binary cannot represent fractions at all
explanation: A reduced fraction terminates in base b exactly when every prime factor of its denominator divides b. Base two has only the factor 2, and 10 = 2 x 5. One tenth is perfectly rational — it repeats in binary for the same reason one third repeats in decimal. The 52-bit answer confuses the symptom with the cause: more bits would not help, just as more decimal digits never finish one third.
